nodes.title: Relational database concepts
nodes.why: Understanding tables and relationships is needed to query and model the historian and outage data sources.
checkpoints: A primary key uniquely identifies each row in a table.
Foreign keys enforce referential integrity between tables.
Normalization reduces redundancy by separating data into related tables.

nodes.title: Programming fundamentals
nodes.why: Basic coding concepts are required to manipulate data with Python and pandas scripts.
checkpoints: Variables store data values that can be read and modified during execution.
Control flow statements like loops and conditionals determine which code runs.
Functions encapsulate reusable logic and can return results to callers.

nodes.title: Statistics fundamentals
nodes.why: Statistical concepts such as error metrics and seasonality are used to evaluate forecast performance.
checkpoints: Mean absolute error averages absolute differences between predicted and observed values.
Seasonality refers to regular, periodic fluctuations in a time series.
Standard deviation measures spread of data around the mean.

nodes.title: SQL queries
nodes.why: The analyst must retrieve and combine load, generation, and outage records from database tables.
nodes.quote: Write SQL queries against our historian
checkpoints: An INNER JOIN returns rows only when matching keys exist in both tables.
GROUP BY aggregates rows sharing a column value, allowing aggregate functions per group.
A WHERE clause filters rows before grouping, affecting which data is aggregated.
Using indexes on join columns speeds up query execution by reducing row scans.

nodes.title: Python pandas
nodes.why: Python with pandas is used to clean, transform, and analyze time‑series data for reporting.
nodes.quote: working knowledge of Python with pandas
checkpoints: The read_csv function loads tabular data into a DataFrame, parsing delimiters automatically.
The .groupby method groups rows by column values and applies aggregate functions.
.fillna replaces missing values with specified constants or methods like forward fill.
Vectorized operations on DataFrames execute without explicit Python loops, improving performance.

nodes.title: Time‑series data cleaning
nodes.why: Cleaned data ensures accurate load and outage analysis despite gaps, meter errors, and clock changes.
checkpoints: Interpolation can fill missing timestamps by estimating values between known points.
Detecting meter errors often involves flagging spikes that exceed typical variance thresholds.
Adjusting timestamps for daylight saving requires shifting affected records by one hour.
Resampling converts five‑minute data to hourly aggregates by applying functions like mean.

nodes.title: Power BI dashboard development
nodes.why: Dashboards deliver real‑time insights to operators and planners in an accessible visual format.
nodes.quote: Build and maintain Power BI dashboards
checkpoints: Power BI visuals update automatically when underlying query results change.
Data slicers let users filter all visualizations on a report page simultaneously.
Publishing a dashboard creates a shared link that respects row‑level security settings.
Drill‑through actions enable users to navigate from summary to detailed data.

nodes.title: Load forecast evaluation
nodes.why: Comparing forecasted and actual load identifies mismatches that must be explained to stakeholders.
nodes.quote: Compare forecast load with actual load
checkpoints: Calculating MAE subtracts forecast from actual, takes absolute value, then averages across periods.
Large forecast errors often coincide with sudden weather changes affecting demand.
Correlation analysis can reveal systematic bias where forecasts consistently overpredict.
Visualizing forecast vs actual with a line chart highlights deviation patterns over time.

nodes.title: Metric documentation
nodes.why: Clear documentation lets other analysts reproduce calculations and understand metric definitions.
nodes.quote: Document every metric so another analyst
checkpoints: A metric definition must list source tables, calculation steps, and aggregation level.
Version control of documentation allows tracking changes and reverting to prior metric logic.
Including example input and output helps readers validate the metric implementation.
Using consistent naming conventions avoids confusion between similarly named metrics.

nodes.title: Power‑grid supply‑demand
nodes.why: Understanding how generation and load are balanced informs analysis of grid performance and outages.
nodes.quote: supply and demand are balanced on a power grid
checkpoints: Supply must equal demand plus losses at every instant to maintain grid frequency.
Dispatch decisions prioritize low‑cost generation sources while respecting transmission constraints.
Imbalance charges are applied when actual generation deviates from scheduled amounts.
Reserve capacity is held to handle unexpected outages or demand spikes.

nodes.title: Technical writing
nodes.why: Clear, non‑technical explanations are required for metrics, reports, and documentation meant for non‑analysts.
nodes.quote: Clear writing for people who are not analysts
checkpoints: Plain language replaces jargon with common terms to improve reader comprehension.
Structured documents use headings, lists, and tables to organize information logically.
Consistent tense and active voice make explanations clearer and more direct.
Providing a summary at the beginning gives readers a quick overview of content.

nodes.title: SCADA data handling
nodes.why: SCADA data provides high‑frequency operational measurements useful for detailed grid analysis.
checkpoints: SCADA tags represent real‑time measurements identified by unique point IDs.
Historian tables store timestamped SCADA values, often at one‑second intervals.
Data extraction queries must filter by tag ID and time range to retrieve relevant records.
Aggregating high‑frequency SCADA data to hourly intervals reduces storage and improves analysis speed.

nodes.title: Weather data analysis
nodes.why: Weather variables help explain load variations and improve forecasting accuracy.
nodes.quote: experience with SCADA data or weather data
checkpoints: Temperature and wind speed forecasts can be merged with load data using timestamp joins.
Correlating precipitation with demand helps explain deviations during extreme weather events.
Normalizing weather variables removes unit differences before regression modeling.
Visualizing weather trends alongside load highlights potential causal relationships.
